decisions.intent: Prevent a TypeError when the table resize control or its parent element is absent while the mouse moves over a table cell, and keep the resize action aligned with the table only when the control exists.

preconditions: The mouse moves over a table cell inside a non-embed table block whose cursor is not col-resize.
The block may or may not have a .table__resize element.
stateTransitions: When .table__resize and its parent exist, the resize action element left is set from the table offset for center/right aligned tables and cleared otherwise.
When .table__resize or its parent is missing, the alignment adjustment is skipped safely.
outputs: The resize action element tracks the table alignment only when the control exists.
Mouse movement over a table cell never throws when the resize control is absent.
invariants: The existing contenteditable column-resize branch keeps its prior behavior.
No unrelated table or gutter logic is changed.
failures: A missing resize control or parent element results in no alignment update rather than an uncaught TypeError.

testEvidence: ESLint on the affected file reports only the pre-existing max-lines-per-function error (215->216 lines), no new diagnostic; stable patch ID matches upstream.
notes: Upstream stable patch ID 22fa20f18ab52f5977e07723d25bde6e74564f09 matches the local diff, so this is a ported-exact port. The max-lines-per-function error predates this port (HEAD also reports 215 lines).
